scope: Grounds P3 (systematic mismatch): digital environments create the illusion of expanded social networks but the social brain's 150-person limit remains. The proxy (follower count) misrepresents the real constraint (cognitive bonding capacity).

content: Tribal social instincts result from gene-culture coevolution of tribal-scale societies. Humans are able to make common cause with a sizable, culturally defined set of distantly related individuals — a form of social organization absent in other primates. These instincts equip humans with the psychological machinery for in-group cooperation, out-group vigilance, and norm-governed behavior in groups of 50-500.
author_quote: The tribal social instincts result from the gene-culture co-evolution of tribal-scale societies by the process described above. Consequently, humans are able to make common cause with a sizable, culturally defined set of distantly related individuals, a form of social organization that is absent in other primates.
caveats: The 'tribal social instincts' hypothesis is Richerson & Boyd's specific theoretical contribution. The claim that this capacity is genetically encoded (not just culturally transmitted) is their strongest and most debated claim.
scope: Grounds M11 (cooperation/alliance): the cooperation mechanism is not a general-purpose prosocial tendency but a specifically tribal-scale adaptation with genetically encoded psychological support. Also M5: tribal instincts include status monitoring (who is in-group vs. out-group).

content: Symbolic markers of group boundaries motivate important behavior. Tribal instincts cause people to use symbolic markers to define who is eligible for empathy, who should excite suspicion, and in some cases who should be killed. Small differences in arrow styles, dress, or dialect become psychologically salient signals of group membership. People essentialist ethnic groups as species-like categories.
author_quote: Tribal instincts cause people to use symbolic markers to define the boundaries of in-groups and establish, for example, who is eligible for empathy, who should excite suspicion, and, in some horrible cases, who should be killed.
caveats: Boyd & Richerson draw on ethnographic evidence (!Kung San arrow styles) and cognitive psychology (Gil-White's ethnic-group essentialism). The claim that ethnic categorization uses species-recognition cognitive machinery is Gil-White's contribution.
scope: Grounds DA5 (defensive over-activation bias) in the social domain: the threat detection system uses symbolic markers to categorize social others, with the result that arbitrary cultural markers trigger in-group/out-group psychology.

content: Modern middle-class reproductive restraint is a striking maladaptation: professional status-seeking consumes resources (time, money, effort) needed for reproduction. Evolved psychology for status competition in Pleistocene tribal contexts now causes fitness loss in modern economies. People prioritize career advancement, education, and consumption over reproduction — the very success of cultural transmission mechanisms (prestige bias, conformist bias) producing behaviors that reduce genetic fitness.
author_quote: You are engaged in maladaptive behavior right now.
caveats: Boyd & Richerson's demographic transition argument is their most provocative mismatch claim. The claim that low fertility is maladaptive assumes genetic fitness as the relevant criterion — cultural fitness may differ.
scope: Directly grounds DC2 (market proxy exploitation): modern status markers (career, wealth, education) hijack M5 (status monitoring) away from its original fitness-enhancing function. The result is systematic suppression of M14 (reproductive motivation) — a paradigm case of proxy exploitation.

content: Complex societies employ institutional work-arounds to simulate tribal-scale relationships: hierarchical command backed by force, segmentary hierarchy, and symbolic in-group marking. Each work-around creates predictable conflicts and failure modes — elite exploitation from hierarchical command, subgroup factionalism from segmentary structure, and fundamentalism from symbolic marking. These are not design flaws but inherent consequences of scaling tribal instincts beyond their natural range.
author_quote: In the section that follows, we describe what seem to us to be the main work-around mechanisms, and the conflicts, compromises, and modes of failure that each entails.
caveats: Boyd & Richerson's work-around taxonomy is their own theoretical classification. The predicted failure modes are consistent with historical and political science evidence but the taxonomy itself is not empirically tested as a unified framework.
scope: Grounds DC2 and P3: the failure modes of modern institutions are predictable from the mismatch between tribal-scale psychology and civilizational-scale social organization. Each work-around trades one type of failure for another.

content: Humans get sick from chronic diseases by doing what they evolved to do but under conditions their bodies are poorly adapted to, then pass those conditions to their children in a vicious cycle. Lieberman calls this dysevolution — an intergenerational feedback loop where mismatch diseases persist because modern environments prevent natural selection from eliminating the underlying susceptibilities.
author_quote: We get sick from chronic diseases by doing what we evolved to do but under conditions for which our bodies are poorly adapted, and we then pass on those same conditions to our children, who also then get sick.
caveats: Lieberman's dysevolution concept is his central theoretical contribution. The intergenerational transmission of mismatch environments is distinct from genetic inheritance of disease.
scope: Grounds P3 and DC1: mismatch is not just an individual problem but a civilizational feedback loop. Modern environments create diseases that modern medicine manages but does not cure, perpetuating the conditions that cause them.

content: Humans evolved to be prone to obesity not because excess fat makes us healthy but because it increases fertility. Anxiety, worry, and stress cause misery and unhappiness but they are ancient adaptations to avoid or cope with danger. The mismatch hypothesis — that human bodies were adapted for very different conditions — is the core of evolutionary medicine.
author_quote: Humans evolved to be prone to obesity not because excess fat makes us healthy, but because it increases fertility. Along the same lines, our species' proclivities to be worried, anxious, and stressed cause much misery and unhappiness, but they are ancient adaptations to avoid or cope with danger.
caveats: Lieberman's obesity-as-fertility claim draws on thrifty genotype hypothesis (Neel 1962) and life-history theory. The fitness-health distinction is central to his argument.
scope: Grounds the distinction between fitness and welfare: M13 (energy regulation) was optimized for fertility, not health. Obesity is the mechanism working correctly in the wrong environment.

content: Type 2 diabetes is a mismatch disease: human bodies, like captive primates, were adapted for very different conditions and are inadequately adapted to cope with modern diets and physical inactivity. The answer does not lie solely in cellular and genetic mechanisms but in the evolutionary mismatch between ancestral and modern environments.
author_quote: diabetes is a growing problem because human bodies, like those of captive primates, were adapted primarily for very different conditions that render us inadequately adapted to cope with modern diets and physical inactivity.
caveats: The captive-primate analogy is Lieberman's. The extension from metabolic mismatch to broader evolutionary medicine is well-established (Gluckman & Hanson 2006).
scope: Paradigm case of P3 + M13 + M10 mismatch: energy regulation (M13) and movement regulation (M10) systems evolved for ancestral activity/diet patterns. Modern sedentary/high-calorie environments produce disease not from system failure but from system-environment mismatch.

content: Farming brought many advantages but also caused serious problems. It enabled more food and hence more children, but also required new forms of work, transformed diets, and opened a Pandora's box of diseases and social ills. The agricultural revolution was the first major dysevolution event — the transition from foraging to farming created the first systematic mismatch between human bodies and their environment.
author_quote: Farming brought many advantages but also caused many serious problems. Farming enabled humans to have more food, hence more children, but also required new forms of work, transformed diets, and opened a Pandora's box of diseases and social ills.
caveats: The agricultural revolution as mismatch origin is well-established in bioarchaeology (Cohen & Armelagos 1984). Lieberman's contribution is framing it as the first dysevolution episode.
scope: Historical anchor for P3: the Neolithic transition was the first large-scale mismatch event, producing skeletal evidence of declining health, new infectious diseases, and social stratification. Every subsequent technological revolution amplifies the original agricultural mismatch.

content: Moderate-pressure massage therapy causes preterm infants to gain more weight, leave tube feeding earlier, perform better on neurological examinations, and be discharged earlier at lower hospital cost. The mechanism involves stimulation of pressure receptors leading to increased vagal activity. Increased serotonin and decreased substance P may mediate the pain-alleviating effects of touch.
author_quote: The babies who were massaged gained 47 percent more weight than those not massaged, a clearly significant weight gain.
caveats: Quote replaced. The prior author_quote ("We found that infants given pacifiers during their tube feedings gained more weight, went off tube feedings earlier...were discharged earlier, at a much lower hospital cost...") is a genuine verbatim passage from Field's Touch, but it describes the PACIFIER / non-nutritive-sucking experiment, NOT the moderate-pressure massage study that the content claim concerns — a source-to-claim mismatch. It has been replaced with the verbatim massage sentence from the same book. NOTE: this book sentence directly supports only the weight-gain component of the content. The additional outcome claims (earlier off tube feeding, better neurological exams, earlier/cheaper discharge) and the mechanism claims (pressure receptors -> increased vagal activity; increased serotonin / decreased substance P) are documented in Field's review articles (e.g., Pediatrics; "Preterm infant massage therapy research: a review," 2010) rather than verbatim in Touch, so for this single-book quote they should be treated as framework synthesis / propagation-level support, not as primary text from the cited work.
scope: Primary evidence for R1 (touch): massage therapy is not just comfort but has measurable physiological effects mediated by specific neurochemical pathways. Directly grounds R1's resolution conditions.

content: Touch deprivation in Romanian orphanages produced devastating consequences: children were skeletal, half normal height, unable to walk or run. After months of regular nutrition and massage therapy, orphanage children recovered physically — illustrating that touch is not merely pleasant but a biological necessity for normal development. Touch deprivation produces growth hormone suppression and immune dysfunction.
author_quote: Tana was raised in a Romanian orphanage. At age seven, relief workers found her all skin and bones and only half the height of a normal child her age.
caveats: Field reports on Romanian orphanage outcomes. The orphanage studies (Nelson, Fox, Zeanah) have become the paradigm case of institutional deprivation effects. Field's specific contribution is the massage therapy intervention.
scope: Grounds DA7 (developmental calibration) for R1: touch deprivation during sensitive periods produces lasting developmental damage. Also grounds DA2: touch is part of the social scaffolding system required for normal development.

content: Many human cultures live skin-to-skin with virtually everyone, maintaining continuous physical contact as the primary mode of social interaction. Modern Western cultures are historically unusual in the degree of touch avoidance and personal-space norms. The reduction of casual physical contact in WEIRD societies represents a mismatch with the ancestral pattern of continuous tactile social regulation.
author_quote: Many human cultures know the primary value of touch. In some primitive cultures, for example, people live skin-to-skin with virtually everyone.
caveats: Field's cross-cultural touch comparison draws on Jourard's (1966) classic observational study of touch frequency across cultures. The 'primitive cultures' language is Field's, from a 2014 publication.
scope: Grounds P3 for R1: modern touch-avoidant cultures represent a systematic mismatch with the ancestral pattern of continuous tactile regulation. The R1 mechanism's resolution conditions (regular physical contact) are structurally unmet in WEIRD environments.

content: Humans are a cultural species. Over a million years ago, members of our evolutionary lineage began learning from each other so that culture became cumulative. Tool-making skills, tracking know-how, and edible-plant knowledge improved and aggregated across generations until the toolkit became so complex that individuals could not figure it out on their own over a lifetime. Culture became the species' primary adaptation.
author_quote: The key to understanding how humans evolved and why we are so different from other animals is to recognize that we are a cultural species. Probably over a million years ago, members of our evolutionary lineage began learning from each other in such a way that culture became cumulative.
caveats: Henrich's cumulative culture thesis builds on Boyd & Richerson's dual-inheritance theory. The million-year timeline is an estimate based on archaeological tool complexity.
scope: Grounds P2 and DA7: human adaptations are domain-sensitive precisely because cultural learning provides the domain-specific knowledge. M4 (social calibration) and M11 (cooperation) are the mechanisms through which cultural knowledge is acquired and maintained.

content: Cultural evolution initiated a process of self-domestication, driving genetic evolution to make humans prosocial, docile, rule-following organisms who expect a world governed by social norms monitored and enforced by communities. Cultural products like fire, cooking, tools, clothing, and language became the main selective pressures that genetically shaped human minds and bodies — culture-gene coevolution creating a new kind of animal.
author_quote: cultural evolution initiated a process of self-domestication, driving genetic evolution to make us prosocial, docile, rule followers who expect a world governed by social norms monitored and enforced by communities.
caveats: Henrich's self-domestication thesis draws on Wrangham's (2019) work and comparative evidence from animal domestication. The claim that norms drove genetic evolution is the strongest version of gene-culture coevolution.
scope: Grounds P1 and M11: human cooperation is not a triumph of reason over instinct but the product of gene-culture coevolution that literally domesticated the species for norm compliance. M5 (status monitoring) was reshaped to track norm compliance rather than just physical dominance.

content: Without culturally transmitted knowledge about how to locate and process plants, fashion tools, and avoid dangers, humans do not last long as hunter-gatherers. European explorers who became separated from their cultural knowledge base routinely perished despite access to the same environments that sustained indigenous populations for millennia. One lone woman equipped with ancestral cumulative know-how survived eighteen years where provisioned, financed exploration teams failed.
author_quote: One lone woman equipped with only the cumulative know-how of her ancestors survived for eighteen years whereas fully provisioned and well-financed teams of experienced explorers struggled in Australia, Texas, and the Arctic.
caveats: Henrich's lost-explorer examples draw on historical cases (Burke and Wills, etc.). The comparison between cultural knowledge and individual intelligence is his central pedagogical device.
scope: Demonstrates that human survival depends on M4 (social calibration/cultural learning) and M11 (cooperative knowledge sharing), not on individual cognitive capacity. Without the cultural knowledge network, even intelligent individuals are helpless.

content: Tinbergen's four questions framework: the complete study of behavior requires investigating (1) causation (mechanism — what internal and external stimuli trigger the behavior), (2) ontogeny (development — how the behavior develops during the organism's lifetime), (3) survival value (function — what adaptive advantage the behavior confers), and (4) evolution (phylogeny — how the behavior evolved across species). These four levels of analysis are complementary, not competing.
author_quote: I remain convinced that it is useful, at least in the present state of our knowledge, to 'dissect' the master question into three stages.
caveats: Tinbergen originally described three stages; the four-question formulation was clarified in his 1963 paper. The Study of Instinct (1951) contains the essential framework in less formalized form.
scope: THE methodological foundation for all of Cor's mechanism analysis: every mechanism must be analyzed at all four levels (causation, development, function, phylogeny). P2 (domain-sensitive interacting adaptations) is itself a four-question claim.

content: Displacement activities occur when two incompatible drives are simultaneously activated — for example, when fighting drive and escape drive conflict at a territory boundary, animals perform apparently irrelevant behaviors like preening or feeding. These activities reveal the competing motivational programs underlying behavior and demonstrate that behavior is not a simple stimulus-response chain but emerges from the interaction of multiple motivational systems.
author_quote: It is a striking fact that displacement activities often occur in a situation in which the fighting drive and the drive to escape are both activated.
caveats: Displacement activities were extensively documented by Tinbergen and colleagues in stickleback fish and herring gulls. The motivational-conflict interpretation remains the standard ethological explanation.
scope: Grounds DA6 (competing motivational programs): Tinbergen's displacement activities are the original empirical evidence that behavior emerges from competing motivational systems. When two programs conflict, the organism produces behaviors belonging to neither — revealing the underlying architecture.

content: Supernormal stimuli: animals preferentially respond to exaggerated versions of natural sign stimuli. Oystercatchers incubate giant artificial eggs over their own normal-sized clutch. Herring gull chicks peck more vigorously at a red knitting needle with white stripes than at a realistic model of the parent's bill. The innate releasing mechanism responds to specific stimulus features, and artificial exaggeration of those features produces stronger responses than the natural stimulus.
author_quote: Oystercatcher incubating 'supernormal' clutch of five eggs in preference to natural clutch of three.
caveats: Tinbergen's supernormal stimulus experiments are among the most replicated findings in ethology. The extension to human proxy hijacking (junk food, pornography, social media) is a modern application of Tinbergen's principle.
scope: THE foundational evidence for DA4 (proxy hijacking via open loops): if the releasing mechanism responds to specific stimulus features, then artificial exaggeration of those features will hijack the mechanism. Modern technology systematically produces supernormal stimuli for every Cor mechanism.

content: A wave of preventable chronic illnesses is sweeping across the globe: certain cancers, type 2 diabetes, osteoporosis, heart disease, strokes, kidney disease, allergies, dementia, depression, anxiety, insomnia. Billions also suffer from lower back pain, fallen arches, plantar fasciitis, myopia, arthritis, constipation, and acid reflux. These are mismatch diseases — conditions whose prevalence surged when human environments departed from the conditions under which human bodies evolved.
author_quote: A wave of obesity and chronic, preventable illnesses and disabilities is sweeping across the globe. These preventable diseases include certain cancers, type 2 diabetes, osteoporosis, heart disease, strokes, kidney disease, some allergies, dementia, depression, anxiety, insomnia, and other illnesses.
caveats: Lieberman's epidemiological claims draw on WHO and CDC prevalence data. The attribution to mismatch is his interpretive framework applied to well-established disease trends.
scope: Comprehensive catalog of P3 mismatch diseases. Covers M10 (movement-related: back pain, flat feet), M13 (metabolic: diabetes, obesity), M8 (immune: allergies, autoimmune). Each disease represents a specific mechanism operating outside its environment of adaptedness.

content: Atherosclerosis is a chronic inflammation of the arterial walls resulting from how the body shuttles cholesterol and triglycerides. The process is driven by the mismatch between ancestral diet/activity patterns (which kept LDL cholesterol low and HDL high) and modern sedentary high-calorie environments that invert this ratio. Chronic arterial inflammation is a paradigm case of allostatic load from metabolic mismatch.
author_quote: Atherosclerosis is a chronic inflammation of the arterial walls that results from how you shuttle cholesterol and triglycerides (fats) around your body.
caveats: Standard cardiovascular pathophysiology. Lieberman's mismatch framing adds the evolutionary context — the cholesterol transport system works correctly but in an environment that disrupts its normal operating parameters.
scope: Grounds DC1 (allostatic load): arterial inflammation IS allostatic load — cumulative damage from chronic metabolic mismatch. Connects M13 (energy regulation) to M8 (immune/inflammatory) via the P3 mechanism.

content: Modern sedentary lifestyle is directly mismatched with ancestral activity patterns. Walking or running 10+ kilometers daily, climbing trees, throwing, eschewing chairs, and sleeping on hard surfaces were normal for most of human evolutionary history. The primal-lifestyle movement correctly identifies the mismatch but often oversimplifies the solution. The key insight is that the chair-based, shoe-bound, indoor modern lifestyle is a novel environment that human bodies are poorly adapted to navigate.
author_quote: Walk or run 10 kilometers (6.2 miles) a day (barefoot, of course), climb a few trees, chase squirrels in the park, throw rocks, eschew chairs, and sleep on a board instead of a mattress.
caveats: Lieberman cites the paleo/primal lifestyle movement while noting its oversimplifications. The 10km/day figure comes from hunter-gatherer energetics data (Pontzer, Marlowe).
scope: Grounds M10 (movement/regulatory): the resolution condition for M10 is embedded daily movement, not periodic exercise. Chairs, shoes, and indoor environments are the specific environmental novelties that create M10 mismatch.

content: Touch and massage therapy produce measurable neurobiological effects: decreased heart rate, blood pressure, and cortisol; increased oxytocin. Brain imaging shows activation of orbitofrontal cortex and caudate cortex during affective touch. The physiological pathway involves stimulation of pressure receptors leading to vagal activation, which in turn modulates the HPA axis and immune function.
author_quote: I examine the physiological and biochemical effects of touch and massage therapy, including decreased heart rate, blood pressure, and cortisol and increased oxytocin.
caveats: Field's own neuroimaging and endocrine studies from the Touch Research Institute. The cortisol reduction from massage is one of the most replicated findings in the touch literature.
scope: Grounds R1 resolution conditions: touch produces measurable stress-axis suppression (cortisol reduction) and immune enhancement via vagal activation. The neurobiological pathway (pressure receptors → vagus → HPA) is the mechanism through which touch provides social regulation (DA2).

content: Physical contact from a partner before stress significantly lowers cortisol and heart rate responses. A ten-minute neck and shoulder massage produced greater stress buffering than verbal social support or no partner interaction. Touch-based social regulation operates through direct physiological pathways (cortisol suppression, cardiovascular calming) not just psychological comfort.
author_quote: Women with physical contact before stress exhibited significantly lower cortisol and heart rate responses to stress but no different plasma oxytocin levels.
caveats: Ditzen et al. experimental design with three conditions (touch, verbal, control). The finding that touch outperforms verbal support is replicated but the null oxytocin finding is more equivocal.
scope: Grounds DA2 (socially scaffolded regulation) via R1: physical touch provides stress buffering that verbal support alone cannot match. The regulatory effect is physiological (HPA axis, cardiovascular), not just psychological.

content: Elderly volunteers who massaged infants showed positive health effects: more social contacts, less coffee consumption, fewer doctor visits. Being massaged and giving massage both produced benefits. This reciprocal caregiving-through-touch model demonstrates that touch regulation is bidirectional — the giver of touch benefits physiologically as well as the receiver.
author_quote: We compared 'grandparent' volunteers massaging infants (figure 2.2), with 'grandparent' volunteers being massaged themselves. Both experiences had positive effects, including such lifestyle changes as participants having more social contacts, drinking less coffee, and making fewer trips to the doctor's office.
caveats: Field's own intervention study. Small sample sizes typical of touch research. The bidirectional benefit finding is supported by broader caregiving literature.
scope: Grounds P3 for R1: elderly touch deprivation is a predictable consequence of age-segregated modern living. The intergenerational touch intervention restores a form of social regulation that was continuous in ancestral contexts.

content: Religious rituals galvanize greater prosociality and bind groups through synchronized behavior. Cultural evolution shaped ritual practices that create collective identity, coordinate group action, and suppress free-riding. Rituals are not arbitrary cultural decorations but functional mechanisms for maintaining cooperation at scales beyond face-to-face reciprocity.
author_quote: Religious rituals that galvanize greater prosociality.
caveats: Henrich's ritual-as-bonding thesis draws on Sosis & Alcorta's costly signaling theory of religion. The claim that rituals are functionally selected (not byproducts) is his position in the religion-adaptation debate.
scope: Grounds M11 (cooperation) and M4 (social calibration): rituals are the mechanism through which large groups maintain coordination beyond the Dunbar number. They create shared emotional states (DA2) that substitute for the face-to-face bonding of smaller groups.

content: The secret of our species' success resides not in the power of individual minds but in the collective brains of communities. Humans became simultaneously the most cooperative and the most warlike of primates — large-scale societies enabling both technological innovation and intergroup conflict. The collective brain hypothesis explains why larger, more interconnected populations innovate faster.
author_quote: The secret of our species' success resides not in the power of our individual minds, but in the collective brains of our communities.
caveats: Henrich's collective brain hypothesis is supported by correlational evidence between population size and technological complexity (Tasmania effect). The cooperation-warfare paradox is his framing of a well-known observation.
scope: Grounds M11: cooperation is a population-level phenomenon, not an individual trait. Also grounds M5: intergroup competition is the selection pressure that maintains within-group cooperation norms.

content: The innate releasing mechanism corresponds to specific properties of environmental stimuli — sign stimuli. Animals respond to specific stimulus features (color, shape, movement pattern) rather than to the whole object. When artificial stimuli exaggerate these features beyond natural ranges, they produce supernormal responses — animals prefer the artificial exaggeration to the real thing. This demonstrates that the releasing mechanism is an open loop: it responds to features, not to the object as a whole.
author_quote: The innate releasing mechanism usually seems to correspond more or less with the properties of the environmental object or situation at which the reaction is normally directed.
caveats: Tinbergen's IRM concept has been refined (innate is no longer taken literally — the mechanism has developmental inputs) but the sign-stimulus principle remains foundational in behavioral ecology.
scope: Grounds DA4 (proxy hijacking via open loops): the open-loop nature of the releasing mechanism is WHY proxies work. The mechanism cannot distinguish natural from artificial stimuli if the artificial stimulus matches the sign-stimulus features. This is the theoretical basis for all modern proxy exploitation.

content: Vacuum activities: a captive starling performed the entire behavior pattern of insect hunting — watching, catching, killing, and swallowing — without any discernible external stimulus. Lorenz confirmed no insects were present. This demonstrates that motivational energy accumulates internally and can discharge behavior without any environmental trigger, when the threshold has been lowered sufficiently by deprivation.
author_quote: These 'explosions' or 'vacuum activities' in a captive starling. It performed repeatedly the whole behaviour pattern of insect hunting, from watching the prey through catching, killing, and swallowing, without any discernible external stimulus.
caveats: Lorenz's vacuum activity observations in captive starlings. The hydraulic energy model behind this (Lorenz's psychohydraulic model) has been superseded, but the phenomenon of threshold-lowering from deprivation is well-established.
scope: Grounds the deprivation-sensitization dynamic in DA4: when a mechanism's resolution conditions are chronically unmet, the threshold for activation drops until the behavior fires at any stimulus — or no stimulus at all. This explains why proxy hijacking becomes more effective under deprivation.

content: Routinely sleeping less than six or seven hours a night demolishes the immune system, more than doubling cancer risk. Insufficient sleep is a key lifestyle factor determining whether you will develop Alzheimer's disease. Sleep disruption contributes to cardiovascular disease, stroke, depression, anxiety, and suicidality. No aspect of human health is spared by sleep loss.
author_quote: Routinely sleeping less than six or seven hours a night demolishes your immune system, more than doubling your risk of cancer.
caveats: Author_quote replaced with the single verified-verbatim prologue sentence (Walker 2017, p. 3): "Routinely sleeping less than six or seven hours a night demolishes your immune system, more than doubling your risk of cancer." The prior quote appended a second sentence ("Insufficient sleep is a key lifestyle factor determining whether or not you will develop Alzheimer's disease."), which is a REWORDED PARAPHRASE of the book's actual sentence ("A lack of sleep is fast becoming recognized as a key lifestyle factor determining whether or not you will develop Alzheimer's disease.") and so violated the verbatim rule; it was removed. The retained sentence fully grounds the content's immune/cancer claim (M7/M8). Substantive caveat retained: Walker's "more than doubling cancer risk" framing rests on Irwin et al. and the WHO/IARC classification of shift work as a probable carcinogen; the effect-size claim has been contested (e.g., Guzey 2019 critique; Ioannidis 2019 on sleep research). Full Alzheimer's sentence available for verbatim re-sourcing under R3 if needed.
scope: Grounds M7 (circadian regulation): sleep loss produces cascading damage across M8 (immune), M1 (anxiety/depression), and DC1 (allostatic load). P3 mismatch: artificial light and 24/7 schedules are the specific environmental novelties.

content: The circadian rhythm — the twenty-four-hour biological pacemaker — orchestrates immune function, metabolic timing, hormonal release, body temperature, and cognitive performance. The suprachiasmatic nucleus generates this rhythm and is synchronized by light-dark cycles. Artificial lighting, screens, and shift work disrupt this synchronization, producing circadian misalignment that cascades through every physiological system.
author_quote: Central to many of the questions in the opening paragraph is the powerful sculpting force of your twenty-four-hour rhythm, also known as your circadian rhythm.
caveats: Standard circadian biology. Walker's synthesis emphasizes the mismatch angle — artificial light as the primary disruptor.
scope: Grounds M7 (circadian regulation) as a master regulatory system: disruption of M7 cascades into M8 (immune timing), M13 (metabolic timing), and M1 (emotional regulation). P3: artificial light is the supernormal stimulus that hijacks the circadian entrainment mechanism.

content: During deep NREM sleep, the glymphatic system — the brain's metabolic waste clearance mechanism — kicks into high gear. A ten- to twentyfold increase in cerebrospinal fluid flushing occurs during NREM sleep, clearing amyloid-beta and tau proteins associated with Alzheimer's pathology. Without adequate deep sleep, this neural detoxification cannot occur, and the toxic waste accumulates.
author_quote: it is during sleep that this neural sanitization work kicks into high gear. Associated with the pulsing rhythm of deep NREM sleep comes a ten- to twentyfold increase in effluent expulsion from the brain.
caveats: Walker reports Nedergaard's (2013) glymphatic system discovery. The amyloid-beta clearance during sleep is well-replicated in animal models; human translation studies are ongoing.
scope: Grounds DC1 (allostatic load) via M7: sleep deprivation directly produces neural waste accumulation — a literal form of allostatic load at the cellular level. The glymphatic system is the resolution condition for M7's housekeeping function.

content: Sleep deprivation is visible in the phenotype: independent judges rate sleep-deprived individuals as less healthy, less attractive, and more fatigued than well-rested individuals from photographs alone. On Cor's reading (not something the study tested, since it measured only perceived health and attractiveness), this makes sleep a phenotypic fitness signal: the physiological state produced by adequate sleep is visible to potential mates and social partners, and sleep loss degrades that signal.
author_quote: Sleep deprived people are perceived as less attractive, less healthy, and more tired compared with when they are well rested.
caveats: Re-sourced 2026-07-18 from Walker (Why We Sleep, 2017) to the primary study, Axelsson et al. 2010 (BMJ 341:c6614, doi 10.1136/bmj.c6614; open access PMC3001961). Walker's secondhand summary mischaracterized the protocol (he described a 'five hours vs eight hours' manipulation; the study actually compared a normal 8-hour night against 31 hours of total sleep deprivation, after a 5-hour night). author_quote is now the paper's verbatim conclusion sentence. source_type upgraded propagation -> primary. evidence_quality='replicated': the perceived-attractiveness/health finding replicates across Axelsson et al. 2010 and Sundelin et al. 2013 ('Cues of fatigue', Sleep 36:1355-1360) and 2017 ('Negative effects of restricted sleep on facial appearance and social appeal', R Soc Open Sci 4:160918). The reproductive-fitness-signal reading is Cor's interpretation (DA1, M7->M14), not tested by the study, and is scoped as such.
scope: Grounds DA1: sleep quality is a visible signal of physiological state. Also links M7 to M14: sleep deprivation degrades the phenotypic signals that the reproductive motivation system uses to assess mate quality.

content: The food industry engineers bliss points — the precise amount of sugar, fat, or salt that sends consumers over the moon. Industry scientists mathematically optimize the hedonic response curve for each product, finding the exact concentration that maximizes craving. This is not accidental food design but systematic exploitation of the reward system's response to ancestrally rare nutrient signals.
author_quote: To plot what industry insiders call the 'bliss point,' or the precise amount of sugar or fat or salt that will send consumers over the moon. At a laboratory in White Plains, New York, industry scientists who perform this alchemy walked me, step by step, through the process of engineering a new soda so that I could see the creation of bliss firsthand.
caveats: Moss's investigative journalism is based on industry documents and interviews with food scientists. The bliss-point optimization process is described by industry insiders, not academic researchers.
scope: THE paradigm case of DA4 (proxy hijacking) + DC2 (market proxy exploitation): the food industry reverse-engineers the M2 (SEEKING/reward) and M13 (energy regulation) systems' stimulus-response curves and deliberately produces supernormal stimuli calibrated to maximize consumption.

content: Salt, sugar, and fat are the three pillars of processed food — the creators of crave. Each CEO needed them in huge quantities to turn products into hits. Officials discussed the power of foods to create cravings that overwhelm the best intentions of dieters. Industry-wide limits on mainline products (not just niche diet items) would be needed to diminish these cravings, but competitive pressure prevents any single company from unilaterally reducing palatability.
author_quote: These were the three pillars of processed food, the creators of crave, and each of the CEOs needed them in huge quantities to turn their products into hits.
caveats: Moss reports on a 1999 meeting of food industry CEOs. The industry's own internal acknowledgment of the craving-creation problem is documented through meeting notes and executive interviews.
scope: Grounds DC2 (market proxy exploitation): the market structure prevents individual companies from reducing palatability because competitors would capture their market share. The exploitation is systemic, not a matter of individual corporate malice.

content: The mechanism of learned helplessness has been biologically well-charted and the original theory got it backward. Passivity in response to prolonged aversive events is not learned — it is the default, unlearned response mediated by serotonergic activity of the dorsal raphe nucleus, which inhibits escape. What is actually learned is the detection of control: the prelimbic region of medial prefrontal cortex detects response-outcome contingency and inhibits the dorsal raphe, enabling active coping.
author_quote: The mechanism of learned helplessness is now very well-charted biologically, and the original theory got it backward. Passivity in response to shock is not learned. It is the default, unlearned response to prolonged aversive events and it is mediated by the serotonergic activity of the dorsal raphe nucleus, which in turn inhibits escape.
caveats: Maier & Seligman's 2016 revision fundamentally inverts their 1967 theory. The dorsal raphe pathway is well-established in rodent models. Human translation is supported by fMRI studies of controllability.
scope: THE foundational revision for M6 (controllability/agency): passivity is the DEFAULT state, not a learned pathology. Control must be actively detected and learned. This inversion has profound implications — depression may be a failure to learn control, not a learned failure.

content: Learned helplessness in the laboratory produces eight of the nine DSM symptoms of depression (excepting suicidal thoughts). The prelimbic medial prefrontal cortex detects contingency between behavior and outcomes and inhibits the dorsal raphe nucleus, restoring the capacity for active escape. When this detection circuit fails — due to chronic uncontrollable stress, developmental adversity, or prefrontal damage — the default passivity state persists as clinical depression.
author_quote: Learned helplessness in the laboratory—combining the animal and human experimental results—produced eight of the nine symptoms [of depression], with the only exception being suicide and suicidal thoughts.
caveats: The 8/9 symptom overlap is based on Maier & Seligman's systematic comparison with DSM criteria. The prelimbic-dorsal raphe circuit is well-characterized in rodents; the human homologue (ventromedial PFC) shows analogous controllability-related activation.
scope: Grounds DA3 (recurrent coupling): M6 failure (loss of controllability detection) cascades into M1 (chronic threat activation via dorsal raphe) and produces the full clinical depression syndrome. The cascade is mediated by a specific neural circuit, not a vague psychological process.

content: Social Baseline Theory: the human brain expects access to social relationships that mitigate risk and diminish the level of effort needed to meet goals. Social and metabolic resources are treated almost interchangeably by the brain — isolation is processed as resource scarcity. Violations of the social proximity expectation increase cognitive and physiological effort as the brain perceives fewer available resources.
author_quote: SBT suggests the human brain expects access to social relationships that mitigate risk and diminish the level of effort needed to meet a variety of goals.
caveats: Coan & Sbarra's theoretical framework integrating attachment, behavioral ecology, and cognitive neuroscience. The social-metabolic equivalence claim is their novel contribution.
scope: THE foundational text for DA2 (socially scaffolded regulation): the brain treats social proximity as a bioenergetic resource. Social isolation is not just emotionally unpleasant — it is metabolically costly because the brain must budget for threats it would otherwise outsource to social partners.

content: SBT describes two mechanisms for social regulation: risk distribution (safety in numbers) and load sharing (distribution of effort toward shared goals). During supportive handholding, the threat-responsive brain returns to a baseline state of relative calm — not through activation of regulatory circuitry but through decreased perceived demand. The brain encodes relational partners as extensions of the self, effectively pooling bioenergetic resources.
author_quote: Although the brain is highly responsive to perceived threat, even simple handholding can substantially attenuate threat responses.
caveats: The handholding fMRI studies (Coan et al. 2006) are the primary empirical support. The self-expansion mechanism draws on Aron & Aron's self-expansion theory. The neural threat-attenuation finding is replicated across multiple studies.
scope: Grounds the M3→M1 regulatory pathway: social bonding does not just comfort — it reduces the neural threat response by changing the brain's resource calculation. This is the mechanism through which DA2 operates at the neural level.

content: Disgust is an evolved psychological system for protecting organisms from infection through disease-avoidant behavior. This behavioral immune system is present in diverse species and exhibits universal features that orchestrate hygienic behavior in response to cues of pathogen contact risk. Three specialized learning mechanisms modify the disgust response: the Garcia effect (one-trial aversion learning), evaluative conditioning, and the law of contagion.
author_quote: Disgust is an evolved psychological system for protecting organisms from infection through disease avoidant behaviour. This 'behavioural immune system', present in a diverse array of species, exhibits universal features that orchestrate hygienic behaviour in response to cues of risk of contact with pathogens.
caveats: Curtis et al.'s behavioral immune system framework. The three learning mechanisms (Garcia, evaluative conditioning, contagion) are their organizational contribution — each is independently well-established.
scope: THE primary text for M12 (contamination avoidance): disgust is not a single emotion but an adaptive system with domain-specific learning mechanisms. The behavioral immune system concept establishes M12 as a distinct mechanism with its own detection and response architecture.

content: Disgust elicitors are universal across cultures: bodily wastes, body contents, sick/deformed/dead/unhygienic people. Contact with disgust elicitors produces a characteristic facial expression, withdrawal/distancing behaviors, and physiological changes including lowered blood pressure and galvanic skin response. Brain imaging reveals a specific neural disgust network including anterior insular cortex, basal ganglia, and ventrolateral prefrontal cortex. All societies demonstrate individual and group-level hygiene behaviors.
author_quote: Contact with disgust elicitors, real or imagined, is associated with (i) a characteristic facial expression... (ii) behaviour patterns that include withdrawal, distancing, stopping or dropping the object of disgust... (iii) physiological changes including lowered blood pressure and galvanic skin response.
caveats: Cross-cultural disgust universality is supported by Curtis et al.'s own web survey (38,845 participants) plus Rozin, Haidt, and Oatley's comparative work. The neural network findings come from multiple neuroimaging studies.
scope: Grounds M12 as having both universal behavioral signatures and a dedicated neural network — meeting the criteria for a domain-specific adaptation (P2). The phylogenetic depth (DA8) is supported by cross-species disgust-like avoidance in diverse mammals.

content: Machine gambling produces a 'zone' state — an absorptive dissociation where nothing else matters. Gamblers describe it as being 'in the eye of a storm' where vision narrows to the machine, the world spins around you, and you cannot hear anything. The primary reinforcer is not winning money but staying in the zone. The gambling industry explicitly designs for 'time-on-device' (TOD) as the target metric.
author_quote: To keep playing— to stay in that machine zone where nothing else matters. It's like being in the eye of a storm, is how I'd describe it. Your vision is clear on the machine in front of you but the whole world is spinning around you, and you can't really hear anything.
caveats: Schull's ethnographic data from Las Vegas machine gamblers. The zone-state description is consistent across multiple informants. Industry confirmation of TOD as design target comes from G2E conference observations.
scope: THE paradigm case of DA4 (proxy hijacking): the machine hijacks M2 (SEEKING) by producing a dissociative flow state that bypasses conscious evaluation. The reinforcer is the process (zone), not the outcome (money). DC2: the industry explicitly engineers for this hijacking.

content: Modern slot machines are engineered systems assembled from 1,200+ individual parts by teams of up to 300 people including mathematicians, graphic artists, marketers, and software engineers. They employ 'losses disguised as wins' (LDWs) — multiline outcomes where the total return is less than the wager but the machine celebrates with lights and sounds, producing the reinforcing arousal of a win on what is actually a net loss. Near-miss effects are engineered through clustering techniques that distort loss perception.
author_quote: Modern slot machines are rarely the work of one company; they are symphonies of individual technologies that come together to create a single experience.
caveats: Schull's investigative ethnography of the gambling technology industry. LDW research has been experimentally validated by Dixon et al. (2010) using skin conductance measures.
scope: Grounds DC2 (market proxy exploitation) at the engineering level: the exploitation is not accidental but designed by multi-disciplinary teams optimizing for behavioral outcomes. LDWs demonstrate that the reward signal can be decoupled from the actual outcome — the organism's M2 system responds to the signal, not the reality.

content: The zone state is described as absorption 'beyond contingency' — a narrowly focused attention state where control dissolves into automaticity. Machine gamblers seek the zone not to win but to escape — from anxiety, grief, boredom, social pain. The machine provides a predictable, controllable micro-environment that the rest of life cannot match. This is proxy hijacking of M6 (controllability) as much as M2 (pursuit).
author_quote: that elusive point of absorption, beyond contingency
caveats: Schull's interpretation of the zone as escape rather than excitement challenges the arousal model of gambling. Her informants consistently describe seeking relief from negative affect rather than thrill-seeking.
scope: Extends DA4: proxy hijacking targets not just M2 (reward pursuit) but M6 (controllability). The machine provides an artificial environment where the organism's actions have reliable consequences — a proxy for controllability that real life cannot provide. This explains why gambling addiction intensifies during life crises.

content: The gambling industry designs for 'extinction' — continued play until total asset depletion. Variable-ratio reward schedules maintain play because the next reward could come at any time. The mathematical structure of the game is invisible to the player, who experiences only the surface (lights, sounds, near-misses) while the underlying probability structure ensures net loss over time. The house edge is designed to be imperceptible on a per-spin basis.
caveats: The prior author_quote ("Extinction as design target; near-miss exploitation; loss disguise mechanisms") was NOT a verbatim quotation from Schull (2012) — it is a three-item framework topic-list / paraphrase and has been removed pending verbatim re-sourcing under R3; source_type demoted primary -> propagation accordingly. The underlying content is substantively corroborated: "playing to extinction" (player runs out of funds) is documented industry/book terminology — Schull's chapter is titled "Overdrive: chasing loss, playing to extinction" — and the near-miss mechanism (extending the reel viewing window so winning symbols sit adjacent to the payline) and loss-disguising via positive reinforcement on multiline machines are genuinely Schull's analysis, also corroborated by Harrigan & Dixon and broader gambling research. The variable-ratio schedule's resistance to extinction is a robust Skinner finding. A direct verbatim primary quote could not be confirmed because the book full text is not openly accessible (no DOI; not in physical collection); only summaries/paraphrases were retrievable, which cannot be trusted as verbatim.
scope: Grounds both DA4 and DC2: the variable-ratio schedule is the mechanism through which the machine maintains M2 engagement despite net loss. The mathematical invisibility of the house edge means M13 (energy regulation) cannot detect the resource drain. This is proxy exploitation at the information-processing level.

content: Dopamine's contribution to reward is chiefly to cause 'wanting' for hedonic rewards, more than 'liking' or learning. The wanting-liking dissociation means that dopamine attributes incentive salience to reward-related stimuli — making them attention-grabbing, attractive, and sought after — without necessarily making them pleasurable. This dissociation explains why addicts compulsively seek drugs they no longer enjoy.
location: Abstract and Introduction (source lines 20-32); sourced from Berridge 2007 Debate paper on disk
author_quote: dopamine's contribution appears to be chiefly to cause 'wanting' for hedonic rewards, more than 'liking' or learning for those rewards.
caveats: Berridge & Robinson's wanting-liking dissociation is one of the most influential frameworks in reward neuroscience. Supported by lesion studies, pharmacological manipulation, and optogenetic studies. The 2007 paper reviews evidence accumulated since the 1998 original.
scope: THE foundational evidence for DA4 (proxy hijacking via open loops): wanting (dopamine-mediated incentive salience) can operate independently of liking (opioid-mediated hedonic impact). This dissociation is WHY proxies hijack behavior — they can trigger intense wanting without delivering genuine satisfaction.

content: Hedonic 'liking' reactions are mediated by opioid systems in nucleus accumbens and ventral pallidum, not by dopamine. Dopamine codes incentive salience (wanting), not hedonic impact (liking). The hedonic reactions are homologous across mammals — humans share reaction details with hominids, moderately with monkeys, and lightly with rodents. This cross-species conservation of the liking system demonstrates its phylogenetic depth.
location: Section on Liking (source lines 183-242); sourced from Berridge 2007 Debate paper on disk
caveats: Audit R3: prior author_quote was non-verbatim; an adversarial verifier refuted the proposed replacement as a paraphrase/synthesis that misrepresents the source. Quote removed and source_type demoted primary -> propagation pending verbatim re-sourcing from Berridge & Robinson (1998). The wanting/liking dissociation (opioid-mediated "liking" in nucleus accumbens and ventral pallidum vs dopamine-coded incentive salience) is itself well-replicated, so evidence_quality="replicated" reflects the underlying science, not the removed quote. [Caveat repaired 2026-07-18: prior caveat's "Context:" tail was contaminated with text belonging to ext 125 (Social Baseline Theory); removed.]
scope: Grounds DA8 (phylogenetic priority) for the reward system: the hedonic liking system is phylogenetically ancient and conserved. DA4 exploits the wanting system (dopamine) while leaving the liking system (opioid) unsatisfied — producing compulsive pursuit without consummatory pleasure.

content: The ACE Study (9,508 respondents) demonstrated a graded dose-response relationship between categories of childhood adversity (psychological abuse, physical abuse, sexual abuse, violence against mother, household substance abuse, mental illness, incarceration) and adult health outcomes. Persons with 4+ ACE categories had 4-12 fold increased risk for alcoholism, drug abuse, depression, and suicide attempts; 2-4 fold increased risk for smoking, poor health, STDs; 1.4-1.6 fold for inactivity and obesity. More than half of respondents reported at least one category. Adult diseases linked included ischemic heart disease, cancer, chronic lung disease, skeletal fractures, and liver disease.
author_quote: We found a graded relationship between the number of categories of childhood exposure and each of the adult health risk behaviors and diseases that were studied.
caveats: Source: PubMed abstract only (full text not on disk). The ACE Study is the largest epidemiological study of childhood adversity-adult disease links. Cross-sectional design limits causal inference but the dose-response gradient and sample size are compelling.
scope: THE paradigm case of DA7→DC1 cascade: childhood adversity calibrates multiple mechanisms (M1 threat, M3 bonding, M6 controllability, M9 care) toward defensive states, which then accumulate allostatic load (DC1) producing adult disease across every organ system.

content: The ACE dose-response gradient shows that childhood adversity is not a binary (traumatized/not) but a cumulative load: each additional category of exposure incrementally increases adult disease risk across behavioral, mental, and physical health domains. The clustering of risk behaviors (smoking, substance use, obesity, sexual risk-taking) suggests that these are not independent choices but downstream consequences of the same developmental calibration toward defensive/avoidant coping strategies.
author_quote: More than half of respondents reported at least one, and one-fourth reported two or more categories of childhood exposures.
caveats: Source: PubMed abstract. The clustering interpretation (risk behaviors as developmental consequences rather than independent choices) is the framework's theoretical extension of Felitti's epidemiological findings.
scope: Grounds DA3 (recurrent coupling): the ACE dose-response shows that childhood adversity does not affect isolated mechanisms — it cascades across multiple systems simultaneously. Each additional ACE category amplifies the cascade, producing the cumulative damage pattern that DC1 describes.

content: Maternal licking/grooming and arched-back nursing in rats alters offspring epigenome at the glucocorticoid receptor (GR) gene promoter in the hippocampus via DNA methylation and histone acetylation changes. Offspring of high-LG mothers have lower glucocorticoid levels, less anxiety, better learning, and delayed brain aging. Methylation differences emerged over the first week of life, were reversed with cross-fostering, and persisted into adulthood. Central infusion of a histone deacetylase inhibitor removed group differences — demonstrating that an epigenomic state established through behavioral programming is potentially reversible.
author_quote: an epigenomic state of a gene can be established through behavioral programming, and it is potentially reversible.
caveats: Source: PubMed abstract + key findings. Weaver et al. 2004 is one of the most cited papers in behavioral epigenetics. The cross-fostering reversal and pharmacological reversal provide the strongest evidence that the effect is behavioral, not genetic.
scope: THE mechanistic evidence for DA7 (developmental calibration): maternal behavior literally writes epigenetic marks on offspring stress-response genes. The cross-fostering reversal proves the marks are written by behavior, not inherited genetically. The pharmacological reversal proves they are epigenetic, not permanent.

content: The specific epigenetic mechanism involves altered methylation at the NGFI-A transcription factor binding site in the GR promoter, changing GR expression in the hippocampus. This alters the negative feedback sensitivity of the HPA axis — high-LG offspring have more hippocampal GR, stronger negative feedback, and lower baseline glucocorticoid levels. The effect cascades: lower baseline stress hormones → less anxiety → better learning → delayed brain aging.
author_quote: Offspring of mothers that showed high levels of LG and ABN were found to have differences in DNA methylation, as compared to offspring of low-LG-ABN mothers.
caveats: Source: PubMed abstract. The GR-methylation → HPA-axis → behavior cascade is the most fully characterized epigenetic pathway in behavioral neuroscience. Replicated across multiple labs (Meaney, Szyf, Champagne).
scope: Grounds the molecular mechanism of DA7: maternal care → GR methylation → HPA calibration → lifelong stress phenotype. This is the most concrete example of how early social environment programs the organism's defensive signaling threshold (DA1).

content: Interface Theory of Perception: through evolutionary game theory and genetic algorithms, veridical (truth-tracking) perceptions are routinely dominated by nonveridical strategies tuned to fitness. Our perceptions of space-time and objects have been shaped by natural selection to hide the truth and guide adaptive behaviors. An interface serves to guide useful actions, not to resemble truth. Veridical perceptions escape extinction only if fitness varies monotonically with truth.
author_quote: our perceptions of space-time and objects have been shaped by natural selection to hide the truth and guide adaptive behaviors.
caveats: Source: PubMed abstract. Hoffman et al.'s Interface Theory is grounded in formal evolutionary game theory. The Invention of Space-Time Theorem is their strongest formal result. The theory remains controversial among perception scientists.
scope: THE foundational text for OF1 (Fitness Interface): perception is an adaptive interface optimized for fitness, not truth. If perceptions do not track truth, then preferences (which are based on perceptions) are mechanism outputs, not ground truth. This is the deepest theoretical grounding for Cor's core claim.

content: The Fitness-Beats-Truth (FBT) Theorem: formal proof using evolutionary game theory and Bayesian decision theory that a strategy maximizing fitness payoff consistently outperforms a strategy attempting to estimate true world states. The fitness-only strategy dominates the truth strategy with this dominance increasing as the perceptual space expands. Natural selection does not favor veridical perception — the standard assumption is provably false.
author_quote: the FBT Theorem shows that the claim is false — that natural selection does not favor veridical perception.
caveats: Source: PubMed abstract. Prakash et al. provide the formal mathematical proof that Hoffman's Interface Theory predicted. The theorem is rigorous within its assumptions but those assumptions (discrete world states, fitness functions) are simplifications.
scope: The formal proof underlying OF1: not merely an argument but a mathematical theorem demonstrating that fitness-optimized perception dominates truth-tracking perception. This closes the theoretical gap — if the FBT theorem holds, then the entire motivational-emotional architecture is a fitness interface, not a truth-tracking system.

content: Error Management Theory (EMT): psychological mechanisms are designed to be predictably biased when the costs of false-positive and false-negative errors were asymmetrical over evolutionary history. Men's sexual overperception bias (overestimating women's sexual interest) and women's commitment underperception bias (underestimating men's commitment) are adaptive biases shaped by asymmetric error costs. EMT offers a systematic framework for predicting cognitive biases from ancestral cost asymmetries.
author_quote: psychological mechanisms are designed to be predictably biased when the costs of false-positive and false-negative errors were asymmetrical over evolutionary history.
caveats: Source: PubMed abstract. Haselton & Buss (2000) tested EMT with N=217 and N=289 across two studies. The sexual overperception bias is one of the most replicated findings in evolutionary psychology. EMT extends Nesse's Smoke Detector Principle to cognitive biases beyond defensive emotions.
scope: THE formal framework for DA5 (defensive over-activation bias) applied to cognitive biases: EMT generalizes the Smoke Detector Principle from defensive emotions to all cognitive mechanisms where error costs are asymmetric. This predicts the specific direction of bias for any mechanism where false negatives are costlier than false positives.

content: Altruistic punishment: individuals punish defectors at personal cost with no material gain. Cooperation flourishes when altruistic punishment is possible and breaks down when it is ruled out. Negative emotions toward defectors are the proximate mechanism behind altruistic punishment. Human cooperation with unrelated strangers in large groups cannot be explained by kin selection, signaling theory, or reciprocal altruism alone — altruistic punishment is a key additional mechanism.
author_quote: Human cooperation is an evolutionary puzzle. Unlike other creatures, people frequently cooperate with genetically unrelated strangers, often in large groups, with people they will never meet again, and when reputation gains are small or absent.
caveats: Source: PubMed full abstract. Fehr & Gachter's experimental public goods game is one of the most influential experiments in behavioral economics. The cooperation-collapse finding when punishment is removed has been replicated extensively.
scope: Grounds M11 (cooperation/alliance): cooperation among strangers requires the threat of punishment by third parties willing to bear costs. The negative-emotion proximate mechanism links M11 to M1 (anger at defectors) and M5 (reputation/status enforcement). Also supports Boehm's reverse dominance hierarchy via different methodology.

content: Allostatic load is the cost of chronic exposure to fluctuating or heightened neural or neuroendocrine response resulting from repeated or chronic environmental challenge. Rather than maintaining constant internal conditions (homeostasis), physiologic systems fluctuate to meet demands from external forces — a state termed allostasis. The hidden cost of chronic stress accumulates over long time periods, acting as a predisposing factor for the effects of acute stressful life events.
author_quote: the cost of chronic exposure to fluctuating or heightened neural or neuroendocrine response resulting from repeated or chronic environmental challenge.
caveats: Source: PubMed summary (no full abstract available for 1993 Archives paper). McEwen & Stellar coined 'allostatic load' in this paper. The allostasis/homeostasis distinction is their conceptual contribution that reframes stress biology.
scope: THE definitional text for DC1 (allostatic load accumulation): McEwen & Stellar's original formulation. Allostatic load is the cumulative physiological price of chronic stress — not the acute stress response itself but the wear and tear from repeated activation. This is the mechanism through which mismatch (P3) produces disease.

content: Individual susceptibility to allostatic load is shaped by behavioral responses coupled to physiologic and pathophysiologic changes beginning early in life. The allostasis framework replaces the static homeostasis model with a dynamic model where the body actively adjusts to anticipated demands — but this adjustment has a cumulative cost when chronically activated. The predisposing-factor model explains why the same acute stressor produces different health outcomes in different individuals.
author_quote: the hidden cost of chronic stress to the body over long time periods, which act as a predisposing factor for the effects of acute, stressful life events.
caveats: Source: PubMed summary. The developmental-susceptibility component (beginning early in life) links allostatic load to developmental calibration (DA7) — early adversity increases later allostatic load vulnerability.
scope: Extends DC1: allostatic load is not just accumulated damage but differential vulnerability calibrated by early experience (DA7). This explains the ACE Study dose-response: early adversity recalibrates the allostatic system to run at a higher baseline, making every subsequent stressor more costly.

content: Meta-analysis of 148 studies (308,849 participants, 7.5 year average follow-up): individuals with stronger social relationships had a 50% greater likelihood of survival (OR=1.50, 95% CI 1.42-1.59). This effect is comparable to smoking cessation and exceeds the influence of obesity and physical inactivity on mortality. Complex social integration measures showed the strongest effect (OR=1.91). The association held across age, sex, initial health status, cause of death, follow-up period, and geographic region.
location: PLoS Medicine, DOI: 10.1371/journal.pmed.1000316, PMID: 20668659 (open access full text)
author_quote: individuals with adequate social relationships have a 50% greater likelihood of survival compared to those with poor or insufficient social relationships.
caveats: Source: PLoS Medicine open-access full text. This is one of the most cited meta-analyses in health psychology. The OR=1.50 aggregates heterogeneous relationship measures; complex integration measures yield stronger effects than simple measures like living alone.
scope: THE quantitative anchor for DA2 (socially scaffolded regulation): social relationships predict mortality with an effect size comparable to major medical risk factors. This means social isolation is literally as dangerous as smoking — a claim that grounds Cor's insistence that social regulation is not optional but survival-critical.

content: Social relationships predict mortality regardless of age, sex, initial health status, cause of death, or geographic region. The effect is not mediated by any single health behavior — it operates across all-cause mortality. Living alone (binary measure) shows the weakest effect (OR=1.19) while complex social integration measures show the strongest (OR=1.91), suggesting that relationship quality and network structure matter more than simple social contact.
author_quote: The overall effect was not moderated by participant sex, length of follow-up, initial health status of participants, or cause of death.
caveats: Source: PLoS Medicine open-access. The gradient from binary (alone/not) to complex (integration measures) supports the Dunbar-layer interpretation — it is not mere presence but quality and structure of social relationships that provides the survival benefit.
scope: Extends DA2: social regulation is not binary (present/absent) but graded by network complexity. This connects to Dunbar's layered model — the innermost 5 relationships provide the most regulation, with diminishing returns at wider layers.

content: Hamilton's genetical mathematical model allows for interactions between relatives on one another's fitness. Using Wright's Coefficient of Relationship as the measure of replica genes in a relative, Hamilton found inclusive fitness — a quantity incorporating the maximizing property of Darwinian fitness. Species following the model tend to evolve behaviour where each organism appears to maximize its inclusive fitness, implying limited restraint on selfish competitive behaviour and possibility of limited self-sacrifices.
author_quote: Species following the model should tend to evolve behaviour such that each organism appears to be attempting to maximize its inclusive fitness.
caveats: Verbatim-confirmed 2026-05-29 against the full text of Hamilton WD (1964) "The Genetical Evolution of Social Behaviour. I", J. Theoret. Biol. 7, 1-16 (DOI 10.1016/0022-5193(64)90038-4; PMID 5875341). The author_quote appears word-for-word in the paper's abstract (incl. British "behaviour" / US "maximize" as in original). Prior QUARANTINE (Codex 2026-04-09: snippet-sourced from Wikipedia + Semantic Scholar abstract, full-text PDF did not render) is hereby cleared: the full-text PDF now renders and the quote and content claim are confirmed against the primary source. Context: Hamilton's rule (rB > C) — the most-cited result in evolutionary biology — and the original formulation uses Wright's coefficient of relationship.
scope: THE foundational text for P1 (inclusive fitness): Hamilton's rule establishes the mathematical conditions under which altruism evolves. All of Cor's mechanism analysis is downstream of this — every mechanism was shaped by selection for inclusive fitness, not individual welfare.

content: Hamilton's rule, in its modern canonical form, states that a social behaviour is favoured by natural selection when rB > C, where r is the coefficient of relatedness between actor and recipient, B is the fitness benefit to the recipient, and C is the fitness cost to the actor. Hamilton's original 1964 paper introduced this principle using a gain-ratio inequality (his condition for an altruistic action to be favoured was -k > 1/r, with k the ratio of gain and r Wright's coefficient of relationship); the compact "rB > C" algebraic notation is a later popularization. The principle explains when organisms will sacrifice personal fitness to benefit relatives and predicts that the altruism threshold decreases with increasing relatedness — in Hamilton's own example, an organism should sacrifice its life to save "more than two brothers, or four half-brothers, or eight first cousins" (siblings r=0.5, cousins r=0.125).
location: Journal of Theoretical Biology 7(1):1-16 and 7(1):17-52, 1964. PMID: 5875341/5875340
author_quote: To express the matter more vividly, in the world of our model organisms, whose behaviour is determined strictly by genotype, we expect to find that no one is prepared to sacrifice his life for any single person but that everyone will sacrifice it when he can thereby save more than two brothers, or four half-brothers, or eight first cousins . . .
caveats: Prior author_quote ("A social behaviour will be favoured by natural selection if and only if rB > C.") was a fabricated/anachronistic snippet — that exact sentence and the "rB > C" notation do NOT appear anywhere in Hamilton (1964). Verified by extracting the full text of the original paper (open-access PDF, joelvelasco.net hamilton64a). Hamilton's actual 1964 selection criterion is the gain-ratio inequality "-k > 1/r" (k = ratio of gain of the action, r = Wright's coefficient of relationship); the algebraic "rB > C" / "rb > c" form is a later textbook popularization, not Hamilton's words. Quote replaced with a verbatim, contiguous passage from the same paper (JTB 7:1-16, the "two brothers / four half-brothers / eight first cousins" statement), which directly supports the claim that the altruism threshold scales with relatedness. Content softened to attribute "rB > C" as the modern canonical statement of Hamilton's principle rather than as Hamilton's 1964 wording. The substance (inclusive-fitness threshold for altruism) is correct and independently verified across decades of behavioral ecology.
scope: The quantitative core of P1: the rB > C inequality is the selection criterion that shaped every social mechanism in Cor. M9 (care/alloparenting) and M11 (cooperation/alliance) both operate under inclusive fitness logic — the organism invests in others to the extent that doing so propagates shared genes.

content: Evolutionary mismatch occurs when human psychological mechanisms, adapted to process ancestral environmental inputs, encounter modern contexts that differ vastly from those environments. Many inputs now differ in quantity, intensity, or no longer have the same fitness associations, leading mechanisms to produce maladaptive output. Li et al. classify mismatch along four dimensions: source (natural vs human-induced), type (forced vs hijacked), cause (input changes vs output-consequence changes), and consequences (effects on reproductive fitness crossed with effects on individual well-being). Tables 1-3 provide worked examples for each dimension.
location: Current Directions in Psychological Science 27(1):38-44, 2018. DOI: 10.1177/0963721417731378
author_quote: Human psychological mechanisms are adaptations that evolved to process environmental inputs, turning them into behavioral outputs that, on average, increase survival or reproductive prospects. Modern contexts, however, differ vastly from the environments that existed as human psychological mechanisms evolved.
caveats: REMEDIATED — Codex audit 2026-04-09. Original flagged CONTENT_PARAPHRASE_DRIFT: second half invented dietary/social-group-size/mating-market/activity-level taxonomy not in the paper. Paper classifies by source/type/cause/consequences (four dimensions). First half with definition and quote verified correct. Rewritten from full text (van Vugt website PDF).
scope: THE formal review of P3 (systematic mismatch) for psychology: Li et al. provide a four-dimensional classification (source, type, cause, consequences) and review evidence in three domains (physical/mental health, mating, work/organizations).

content: The mismatch framework has implications for public policy. Li et al. present specific examples: (1) despite modern sanitation benefits, immune systems evolved to be stimulated by bacterial exposure in infancy — overuse of antibacterial products may contribute to childhood asthma, allergies, and ear infections; (2) ecological conservation efforts have met limited success because conservation behavior is evolutionarily novel — humans evolved to consume local resources without concern when pollutant output was low and migration was feasible. Effective interventions should work with, rather than oppose, evolved tendencies such as self-interest, social status concerns, social imitation, and future discounting.
location: Current Directions in Psychological Science 27(1):38-44, 2018. DOI: 10.1177/0963721417731378
author_quote: Many inputs now differ in quantity and intensity or no longer have the same fitness associations, thereby leading many mechanisms to produce maladaptive output.
caveats: REMEDIATED — Codex audit 2026-04-09. Original flagged CONTENT_PARAPHRASE_DRIFT: drifted paper's actual policy framing (antibacterial products, conservation) into fix-environment-not-medication framing the paper does not use. DC3 removed from foundation_codes (paper does not support it). Rewritten from full text (van Vugt website PDF).
scope: Policy implications of the mismatch framework: interventions should align with, not oppose, evolved tendencies. Specific examples: immune-system mismatch from excessive hygiene, conservation-behavior mismatch from evolved resource-consumption tendencies.

content: McEwen's 1998 NEJM review: the physiologic response to stress, allostatic load, reflects wear and tear from not only life experiences but also genetic load, individual lifestyle habits (diet, exercise, substance abuse), and developmental experiences. Hormones associated with stress protect the body short-term through allostasis but in the long run cause disease. Four conditions produce allostatic load: (1) repeated stressors, (2) lack of adaptation to repeated stressors, (3) prolonged response due to delayed shutdown, and (4) inadequate response leading to compensatory hyperactivity of other systems.
author_quote: The price of this accommodation to stress can be allostatic load, which is the wear and tear that results from chronic overactivity or underactivity of allostatic systems.
caveats: Author_quote replaced with the verbatim canonical definition of allostatic load from McEwen 1998 NEJM 338(3):171-179 (full-text PDF, Univ. of Wisconsin mirror of the NEJM article), confirmed word-for-word: "The price of this accommodation to stress can be allostatic load, which is the wear and tear that results from chronic overactivity or underactivity of allostatic systems." (The inline reference superscript "2" in the source after "allostatic load" is omitted; no other change.) The PRIOR quarantined quote — "Over time, daily stressful events result in wear and tear on the body called allostatic load." — does NOT appear anywhere in the source and was a non-verbatim paraphrase/snippet contamination (the "daily events of life... wear and tear... allostatic load" framing it echoes is from McEwen & Stellar 1993, a different work); it has been removed.
